main_residual_risks: A real provider may not satisfy the deterministic capability contract, may return unstable identity evidence, or may need idempotency behavior not exercised by fixtures.
The current dirty worktree may hide an omitted package, fixture, or documentation dependency until M18 runs an isolated install.
At-most-once crash safety deliberately blocks an indeterminate call; it does not prove exactly-once execution of an arbitrary external provider.
overturning_evidence: A replay showing that a topic candidate changes GENESIS, mission ID, or fingerprint.
A crash point that permits a second capability call or exposes effective seeds before pointer selection and journal reconciliation.
A clean-checkout failure caused by an omitted successor-manifest dependency.
A production adapter that cannot preserve confirmation, request lineage, closed outcomes, or fail-closed indeterminate-call handling.
strongest_alternative_explanation: The passing result may reflect a well-specified local state machine and exhaustive fixture crash harness rather than a usable live topic-bootstrap capability.
weakest_evidence: No live provider, source, human-review, clean-install, or independent operator path was exercised in M17.
what_failed_or_did_not_run: The first 502-row successor manifest omitted the actual 1,137 Phase 10 evidence members behind its inventory record; a supervisor audit found the under-closure, expanded the manifest to 1,671 rows, and reran exact replay before M17 close.
The first final full-unit and full-CLI reruns were interrupted by the VS Code crash; their partial logs are preserved as diagnostic-only evidence.
Two ad hoc close-audit one-liners initially used stale JSON/JUnit field assumptions; corrected read-only audits passed and did not change product or canonical test artifacts.
